findings.reason: At src/date/mini.js:22 the new branch is `args[0] instanceof Date`, so a Date from another realm (iframe or vm context) fails it and drops into the else branch at :24-31, which re-applies the local-vs-zone offset and moves the instant. This is an edge case outside the locked same-realm tests, so it stays low.
findings.claim: A Date from another realm fails the instanceof Date check and falls into the date-values branch, so its instant gets shifted by the zone-offset difference instead of being kept.
findings.evidence: `} else if (args[0] instanceof Date) { this.setTime(+args[0]); } else { this.setTime(+new Date(...args)); const offset = tzOffset(this.timeZone, this); const localOffset = -new Date(...args).getTimezoneOffset(); Date.prototype.setMinutes.call(this, ... + (localOffset - offset)); }`. A cross-realm Date is not `instanceof` this realm's Date, so it takes the `else` path, which treats its value as local wall-clock time and re-offsets it. The locked tests (src/date/tests.ts:55-63, 149-151) only use same-realm `new Date(...)`.
